Under the batch rule, readings with no declaring word article are listed but not quizzed. All six cards quiz only their on reading (卑 ヒ, 汰 タ, 沙 サ, 沢 タク, 胡 コ, 鼓 コ). 胡 is not a Joyo kanji (KANJIDIC2 grade 9; Digital Daijisen labels it ［人名用漢字］); the other five quizzed readings are in the official Joyo table.

汰 タイ, おご.る, にご.る and よな.げる, 沙 よなげる, 沢 うるお.い, うるお.す and つや, and 胡 なんぞ have no checked JMdict example and are labelled source-only on the cards; Kanjipedia's 卑 ひくい and 沙 みぎわ, which are not KANJIDIC2 readings, are explained in Notes with no table row.

Some titles share an English word with existing titles in another sense and are not excluded from each other's quiz options, except where a Notes bullet on the card says otherwise; the design check's ten accepted warnings are all 汰's "out" against 出, 吐, 呼, 執, 履, 敷, 施, 滅, 眺 and 裁. The only pair of new cards excluding each other is 汰/沙, declared on 沙; the app's QuizBuilder applies an exclusion in both directions.
Each mnemonic is a modern-shape memory aid, labelled on the card as not etymology; component and stroke statements follow the pinned KanjiVG revision.
The reading audits are the author's Python ports of the Kotlin builder; no Kotlin cross-check was run.
The scope audits do not attribute reads made through shell commands or Python, so they can list files as unread that the reports say were read.

Several judgments rest partly on live reads of Kanjipedia, Digital Daijisen (Weblio) and Jisho pages, not on pinned copies in the packet; both confirmations checked the Joyo table only in the packet's extract.

The confirmation reviewers did not re-run the audits; they judged the check outputs that the author ran on the revised snapshot and included in their packets. confirm-claude took the lint, test, validation, manifest, budget, vocabulary, link-plan and kanji-remarks results from CHANGES.md without opening those outputs.
